subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- N := q + 1, the degree of X and the dimension of its parameter space.
- 𝒟^j := TestFormOn univ j; |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α; ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm (the operator norm for linear maps and covectors).
- e′_a := EuclideanSpace.single a 1 ∈ ℝ^N (a ∈ Fin N) and e_b := EuclideanSpace.single b 1 ∈ ℝ^{N+1} = Euclid (q+1+1) (b ∈ Fin (N+1)). DG_i(u)e′ := (DG_i(u)e′_a)_a.
- For an (N+1)-form ω, Kω(x) := ∫_0^1 t^N • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x dt.
- Coordinates on ℝ^{N+1}: π₀(w) := w 0 ∈ ℝ and π′(w) := WithLp.toLp 2 (Fin.tail (WithLp.ofLp w)) ∈ ℝ^N. Both are continuous linear of norm ≤ 1, with π₀e_0 = 1, π′e_0 = 0, π₀e_{a+1} = 0 and π′e_{a+1} = e′_a.
- Θ(w) := (π₀w, π′w) is a measurable equivalence ℝ^{N+1} → ℝ × ℝ^N carrying Lebesgue measure to the product of the Lebesgue measures. It is the composition of WithLp.ofLp (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), MeasurableEquiv.piFinSuccAbove at 0 (volume_preserving_piFinSuccAbove) and WithLp.toLp on the second factor (PiLp.volume_preserving_toLp).

1. Radius and retraction.
 - spt X is compact; choose ρ > 0 with spt X ⊆ ball(0, ρ). Then ‖G_i(u)‖ < ρ for u ∈ A_i, because G_i(A_i) ⊆ spt X.
 - Let φ be the ContDiffBump centered at 0 with rIn = ρ and rOut = ρ + 1, and put r(y) := φ(y)•y. Then r is C^∞ with compact support. Hence r is Lipschitz (ContDiff.lipschitzWith_of_hasCompactSupport) and bounded, ‖r(y)‖ ≤ ρ + 1, and r(y) = y for ‖y‖ ≤ ρ.
 - Fix L_i with G_i L_i-Lipschitz. Let σ(s) := max(0, min(s, 1)): σ is 1-Lipschitz, |σ| ≤ 1, and σ(s) = s on [0, 1].
2. Definitions. For i ∈ ℕ and w ∈ ℝ^{N+1}:
 - H_i(w) := σ(π₀w) • r(G_i(π′w));
 - B_i := π₀⁻¹(Ioo 0 1) ∩ π′⁻¹(A_i);
 - h_i(w) := w_i(π′w) ∈ ℤ;
 - c′_i(w) := (π₀w)^N · ‖G_i(π′w)‖ · c_i(π′w).
3. Elementary properties.
 (a) H_i is Lipschitz: ‖H_i(w) − H_i(z)‖ ≤ |σ(π₀w) − σ(π₀z)|·‖r(G_i π′w)‖ + |σ(π₀z)|·‖r(G_i π′w) − r(G_i π′z)‖ ≤ ((ρ + 1) + Lip(r)·L_i)·‖w − z‖.
 (b) B_i is Borel, as an intersection of preimages of Borel sets under continuous maps. h_i and c′_i are measurable: compositions of the measurable w_i and c_i with continuous maps, and products of measurable real functions.
 (c) h_i is integrable on B_i: since Θ is measure preserving, Tonelli gives ∫_{B_i} |h_i| = ∫_{Ioo 0 1} ∫_{A_i} |w_i(u)| du ds = ∫_{A_i} |w_i| < ∞, because w_i is integrable on A_i.
4. Derivative of H_i on B_i. Let w ∈ B_i, s := π₀w ∈ (0,1), u := π′w ∈ A_i.
 - The set O := {z : π₀z ∈ Ioo 0 1, ‖G_i(π′z)‖ < ρ} is open (G_i is continuous) and contains w.
 - On O we have σ(π₀z) = π₀z and r(G_i(π′z)) = G_i(π′z). So H_i = H̃_i on O, where H̃_i(z) := (π₀z)•G_i(π′z).
 - G_i is differentiable at u (hypothesis). By the product and chain rules, H̃_i is differentiable at w with DH̃_i(w)(v) = (π₀v)•G_i(u) + s•DG_i(u)(π′v).
 - By Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, DH_i(w) = DH̃_i(w). Hence DH_i(w)e_0 = G_i(u) and DH_i(w)e_{a+1} = s•DG_i(u)e′_a. That is, (DH_i(w)e_b)_b = Fin.cons (G_i u) (a ↦ s•DG_i(u)e′_a), and H_i(w) = s•G_i(u).
5. Evaluation identity. For every (N+1)-covector α and w as in step 4:
 α(DH_i(w)e) = (α.curryLeft (G_i u))(a ↦ s•DG_i(u)e′_a) = s^N·(α.curryLeft (G_i u))(DG_i(u)e′).
 This uses curryLeft_apply_apply and multilinearity in the remaining N slots (map_smul_univ with all factors s, ∏_a s = s^N).
6. The c′ bound. For w ∈ B_i and every (N+1)-covector α:
 |α(DH_i(w)e)| = s^N·|(α.curryLeft (G_i u))(DG_i(u)e′)|
  ≤ s^N·c_i(u)·|α.curryLeft (G_i u)|  (hypothesis on c_i at u ∈ A_i, applied to the N-covector α.curryLeft (G_i u))
  ≤ s^N·c_i(u)·‖G_i u‖·|α|  (sibling curry_le = accepted cmcdt_lp_covector_curryLeft_norm_le with N := P, k := q + 1, v := G_i u, β := α; uses s^N c_i(u) ≥ 0)
  = c′_i(w)·|α|.
 Also c′_i(w) ≥ 0, since s > 0 and c_i(u) ≥ 0.
7. Summability. For each i, Θ and Tonelli (lintegral_prod), with s^N ≤ 1 on (0,1) and ‖G_i u‖ ≤ ρ on A_i, give
 ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(|h_i|·c′_i) = ∫⁻_{Ioo 0 1} ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i(u)|·s^N·‖G_i u‖·c_i(u)) du ds ≤ ofReal(ρ)·∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|·c_i).
 Summing over i (ENNReal.tsum_mul_left): Σ_i ∫⁻_{B_i} ofReal(|h_i|·c′_i) ≤ ofReal(ρ)·Σ_i ∫⁻_{A_i} ofReal(|w_i|·c_i) < ∞.
8. The series for Y. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^{N+1}. By hypothesis there is η ∈ 𝒟^N with η(x) = Kω(x) for x ∈ spt X and Y(ω) = X(η). The HasSum hypothesis for X at γ := η gives HasSum (i ↦ I_i) (X(η)), where I_i := ∫_{A_i} w_i(u)·η(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e′) du. Fix i.
 (a) Inner integral. For u ∈ A_i, G_i(u) ∈ spt X, so η(G_i u) = Kω(G_i u). Evaluation at the fixed tuple DG_i(u)e′ is a continuous linear functional on N-covectors (ContinuousAlternatingMap.apply), so it commutes with the interval integral of the continuous integrand (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm; compiled in Lean during decomposition). With curryLeft_apply_apply:
  η(G_i u)(DG_i(u)e′) = ∫_0^1 t^N·ω(t•G_i u)(Fin.cons (G_i u) (DG_i(u)e′)) dt.
  For t ∈ (0,1) and w := Θ⁻¹(t, u) ∈ B_i, steps 4–5 give ω(H_i w)(DH_i(w)e) = t^N·ω(t•G_i u)(Fin.cons (G_i u) (DG_i(u)e′)). The interval integral over [0,1] equals the integral over Ioo 0 1.
 (b) Integrability. Let F_i(t, u) := w_i(u)·ω(H_i(Θ⁻¹(t,u)))(DH_i(Θ⁻¹(t,u))e).
  - F_i is measurable on (0,1) × A_i: w_i and fderiv are measurable (measurable_fderiv), and ω and G_i are continuous.
  - |F_i(t,u)| ≤ |w_i(u)|·‖ω‖_∞·ρ·L_i^N, with ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x ‖ω(x)‖ < ∞ (ω is continuous with compact support). This uses |α(v)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_b ‖v_b‖, ‖G_i u‖ < ρ, s ≤ 1, and ‖DG_i(u)‖ ≤ L_i (norm_fderiv_le_of_lipschitz).
  - The bound is integrable on (0,1) × A_i because w_i is integrable on A_i. So F_i is integrable.

subproblem.title: Radial homotopy operator: K beta is smooth and beta = d(K beta) + K(d beta)
subproblem.statement:
Let P, q ∈ ℕ and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^{q+1}(ℝ^P) be a C^∞ (q+1)-form (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q+1) with ContDiff ℝ ⊤ β). For x ∈ ℝ^P put (Kβ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^q·ι_x(β(t x)) dt, where ι_xα := α.curryLeft x, i.e. (ι_xα)(v_1, …, v_q) = α(x, v_1, …, v_q). The integral is an interval integral in the finite-dimensional normed space Λ^q(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) q of continuous alternating q-forms. Then:
(1) Kβ : ℝ^P → Λ^q(ℝ^P) is C^∞;
(2) for every x ∈ ℝ^P, d(Kβ)(x) + ∫_0^1 t^{q+1}·ι_x((dβ)(t x)) dt = β(x), where d is the exterior derivative (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv).
This is the homotopy formula β = d K_{q+1}β + K_{q+2} dβ of the Poincaré lemma for the radial contraction (Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26; steps 1–2 of the parent proof).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)), ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) β → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) (fun x : Euclid P => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ q • (β (t • x)).curryLeft x) ∧ ∀ x : Euclid P, exteriorDerivative (fun y : Euclid P => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ q • (β (t • y)).curryLeft y) x + (∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • (exteriorDerivative β (t • x)).curryLeft x) = β x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- Λ^j := Covector (Euclid P) j, the continuous alternating j-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm. It is finite-dimensional, hence complete.
- ι_xα := α.curryLeft x, so (ι_xα)(v_1, …, v_j) = α(x, v_1, …, v_j).
- d = exteriorDerivative = Mathlib extDeriv: dω(x) = alt(Dω(x)), where alt := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin is a continuous linear map (alternatizeUncurryFinCLM) and D := fderiv ℝ.
- h(t, x) := t^q • ι_x(β(t•x)) for (t, x) ∈ ℝ × ℝ^P. So Kβ(x) = ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt.
- K′(dβ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) dt.

1. h is C^∞.
 - (t, x) ↦ t^q and (t, x) ↦ t•x are C^∞, so (t, x) ↦ β(t•x) is C^∞ (composition with the C^∞ map β).
 - Φ : Λ^{q+1} × ℝ^P → Λ^q, Φ(f, z) := f.curryLeft z, is continuous and bilinear: f ↦ f.curryLeft is the linear isometry ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI : Λ^{q+1} → L(ℝ^P, Λ^q), followed by evaluation, which is bounded bilinear. Hence Φ is C^∞.
 - Scalar multiplication ℝ × Λ^q → Λ^q is C^∞.
 So h(t, x) = t^q • Φ(β(t•x), x) is C^∞ on ℝ × ℝ^P.
2. Smoothness and derivative of Kβ. Apply the sibling param_integral (the accepted cmcdt_lpo_slice_param_integral) with N := P, V := Λ^q (a complete real normed space) and h.
 - x ↦ ∫_0^1 h(t, x) dt = Kβ is C^∞. This is conclusion (1).
 - For every x, Kβ has Fréchet derivative D(Kβ)(x) = ∫_0^1 D_x h(t, ·)(x) dt, where D_x h(t, ·)(x) := fderiv ℝ (x′ ↦ h(t, x′)) x = Dh(t, x) ∘L inr.
3. Exterior derivative of Kβ.
 - t ↦ D_x h(t, ·)(x) = Dh(t, x) ∘L inr is continuous, because h is C^1 and so Dh is continuous. Hence it is interval integrable on [0, 1].
 - alt is a continuous linear map, so it commutes with the interval integral (ContinuousLinearMap.intervalIntegral_comp_comm):
 d(Kβ)(x) = alt(∫_0^1 D_x h(t, ·)(x) dt) = ∫_0^1 alt(D_x h(t, ·)(x)) dt = ∫_0^1 d(h(t, ·))(x) dt.
4. Pointwise identity. Fix t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ ℝ^P. Let β_t(y) := β(t•y), which is C^∞, and ψ_t(y) := ι_y(β_t(y)) = (β_t(y)).curryLeft y. Then h(t, ·) = t^q • ψ_t.
 (a) Chain rule. β_t = β ∘ (t • id), so Dβ_t(x) = Dβ(t•x) ∘L (t • id) = t • Dβ(t•x). Applying alt gives dβ_t(x) = t • (dβ)(t•x). Evaluating at x gives Dβ_t(x)[x] = t • Dβ(t•x)[x].
 (b) Cartan's formula. Apply the sibling euler_cartan (the accepted dtc_cone_euler_cartan) with m := q, β := β_t, y := x; β_t is differentiable at x:
 dψ_t(x) + ι_x(dβ_t(x)) = ((q : ℝ) + 1) • β_t(x) + Dβ_t(x)[x].
 (c) d commutes with constant scalars (exteriorDerivative_smul), so d(h(t, ·))(x) = t^q • dψ_t(x). Multiply (b) by t^q and use (a) and curryLeft_smul (ι_x(t•α) = t•ι_xα):
 d(h(t, ·))(x) + t^{q+1} • ι_x((dβ)(t•x)) = ((q : ℝ) + 1)·t^q • β(t•x) + t^{q+1} • Dβ(t•x)[x].   (∗)
 (d) The right side of (∗) is g′(t), where g(t) := t^{q+1} • β(t•x) : ℝ → Λ^{q+1}. Indeed, by the product rule and the chain rule (the derivative of t ↦ t•x is x), HasDerivAt g (((q : ℝ) + 1)·t^q • β(t•x) + t^{q+1} • Dβ(t•x)[x]) t.
 Remark. Expanding both sides of (∗) with exteriorDerivative_apply gives exactly the computation in step 2 of the parent proof. The terms Σ_i (−1)^{i−1} Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, v_1, …, v̂_i, …, v_q) of d(h(t,·))(x)(v) cancel against the terms Σ_i (−1)^i Dβ(tx)[v_i](x, …) of ι_x(dβ)(tx)(v). Cartan's formula packages this cancellation.
5. Integration.

 - Integrate (∗) over [0, 1] and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus (intervalIntegral.integral_eq_sub_of_hasDerivAt with step 4(d)):

 since q + 1 ≥ 1.
6. By steps 3 and 5, d(Kβ)(x) + K′(dβ)(x) = β(x) for every x ∈ ℝ^P. This is conclusion (2). ∎

subproblem.title: The cone current 0 ⨯ X: boundary X, compact support in the cone over spt X, and action ω ↦ X(Kω)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P q : ℕ) (X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1)) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1)), R.Represents X → R.carrier ⊆ X.support → R.measure univ ≠ ∞ → X.boundary = 0 → IsCompact X.support → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1 + 1), Y.boundary = X ∧ IsCompact Y.support ∧ Y.support ⊆ {y : Euclid P | ∃ s ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ x ∈ X.support, y = s • x} ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1 + 1), ∃ η : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (q + 1), (∀ x ∈ X.support, (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1)) x = ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, t ^ (q + 1) • ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (q + 1 + 1)) (t • x)).curryLeft x) ∧ Y ω = X η
subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation.
- k := q + 1 ≥ 1 is the degree of X.
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, H^k := μHE[k].
- 𝒟^j := TestFormOn univ j, the C^∞ compactly supported j-forms.
- ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Λ^j := Covector (Euclid P) j and on k-vectors.
- For a (k+1)-form ω, (Kω)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^k • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x dt, a k-form.
- For a k-form γ, (K₀γ)(x) := ∫_0^1 t^q • (γ(t•x)).curryLeft x dt, a q-form.
- d is exteriorDerivative. For a test form γ, dγ is the test form exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ _ γ, whose underlying form is exteriorDerivative γ.

0. Two properties of X (step 0 of the parent proof).
 (0a) Vanishing. If γ ∈ 𝒟^k and γ(x) = 0 for every x ∈ spt X, then X(γ) = 0. Indeed, since R represents X, X(γ) = R.action γ = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ(x)) dH^k(x). For x ∈ M ⊆ spt X the integrand is θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero).
 (0b) C⁰ bound. Put C_X := (R.measure univ).toReal. By definition R.measure univ = ((H^k⌞M).withDensity θ)(ℝ^P) = ∫⁻_M θ dH^k, which is finite by hypothesis. Claim: if γ ∈ 𝒟^k and b ≥ 0 satisfy ‖γ(x)‖ ≤ b for all x, then |X(γ)| ≤ C_X·b.
  - By R.orients, for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M there are a plane Q and an orthonormal τ = (τ_1, …, τ_k) with ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α (IsUnitOrientationOf).
  - Hence |ξ(x)(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_i ‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
  - So |θ(x)·ξ(x)(γ(x))| ≤ θ(x)·b for H^k-a.e. x ∈ M.
  - θ is measurable with ∫⁻_M θ < ∞, so x ↦ θ(x)·b is integrable on M with integral C_X·b. By norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, |X(γ)| ≤ C_X·b.
1. Cutoff. spt X is compact, hence bounded; choose ρ > 0 with ‖x‖ < ρ for all x ∈ spt X. Let ζ be the ContDiffBump centered at 0 with rIn = ρ and rOut = ρ + 1. Then:
 - ζ is C^∞ with compact support and 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1;
 - ζ(x) = 1 for ‖x‖ ≤ ρ, and ζ(x) = 0 for ‖x‖ > ρ + 1 (tsupport ζ = closedBall 0 (ρ+1));
 - in particular ζ ≡ 1 on the open set N := ball(0, ρ) ⊇ spt X.
 (This construction was compiled in Lean during decomposition.)
2. The test forms η_ω. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}.
 - By the sibling radial_homotopy (with q := k and β := ω, which is C^∞), Kω is C^∞.
 - Hence η_ω(x) := ζ(x) • Kω(x) defines a C^∞ k-form (ContDiff.smul) with tsupport η_ω ⊆ tsupport ζ, which is compact. So η_ω ∈ 𝒟^k.
 - ω ↦ η_ω is ℝ-linear. For fixed x, the integrand t ↦ t^k • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x is continuous, hence interval integrable on [0, 1], and it is linear in ω (curryLeft_add, curryLeft_smul). So K(ω + ω′) = Kω + Kω′ and K(cω) = c·Kω by linearity of the interval integral, and multiplication by ζ keeps linearity.
 - For x ∈ spt X, ζ(x) = 1, so η_ω(x) = Kω(x).
3. The current Y. Define Y(ω) := X(η_ω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}. This is a linear functional: the linear map ω ↦ η_ω of step 2 followed by X.
 Continuity (step 4 of the parent proof; its a = 0 estimate suffices together with (0b)):
 - Let ω_j ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K₁ with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K₁ for all j, and iteratedFDeriv ℝ a ω_j → 0 uniformly on K₁ for every a.
 - Take a = 0. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f y‖ = ‖f y‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every ε > 0 there is J with ‖ω_j(y)‖ ≤ ε for all j ≥ J and y ∈ K₁. For y ∉ K₁, ω_j(y) = 0. So ‖ω_j(y)‖ ≤ ε for all y and all j ≥ J.
 - Let j ≥ J and x ∈ ℝ^P. Then ‖(ω_j(t•x)).curryLeft x‖ ≤ ‖ω_j(t•x)‖·‖x‖ ≤ ε‖x‖ (norm_curryLeft), and 0 ≤ t^k ≤ 1 on [0, 1]. So ‖Kω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε‖x‖ (intervalIntegral.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le_const).
 - Since |ζ| ≤ 1 and ζ(x) = 0 for ‖x‖ > ρ + 1, ‖η_{ω_j}(x)‖ ≤ (ρ + 1)ε for all x.
 - By (0b), |Y(ω_j)| = |X(η_{ω_j})| ≤ C_X(ρ + 1)ε for j ≥ J. Hence Y(ω_j) → 0.
 So (toCurrent := X ∘ (ω ↦ η_ω), continuous′ as above) is a GeometricCurrentOn univ (k+1) = GeometricCurrentOn univ (q+1+1). Call it Y.
4. Action formula. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1}, the test form η := η_ω satisfies η(x) = Kω(x) = ∫_0^1 t^{q+1} • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x dt for x ∈ spt X (step 2), and Y(ω) = X(η) by definition. This is the last conclusion.
5. ∂Y = X (step 5 of the parent proof). Let γ ∈ 𝒟^k = TestFormOn univ (q+1).
 - By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, ∂Y(γ) = Y(dγ) = X(η_{dγ}), where η_{dγ} = ζ • K(dγ) and K(dγ)(x) = ∫_0^1 t^{q+1} • ((dγ)(t•x)).curryLeft x dt.
 - By radial_homotopy (with q and β := γ), K₀γ is C^∞ and d(K₀γ)(x) + K(dγ)(x) = γ(x) for all x. Hence η_{dγ} = ζ•γ − ζ•d(K₀γ) pointwise. (The definitional alignment of K(dγ) with the homotopy formula was compiled in Lean during decomposition.)
 - ζ•γ and ζ•d(K₀γ) are test k-forms: they are C^∞ (d(K₀γ) = alt ∘ D(K₀γ) is C^∞ because K₀γ is) and have tsupport ⊆ tsupport ζ. Likewise ψ := ζ•K₀γ ∈ 𝒟^q.
 - By linearity of X, X(η_{dγ}) = X(ζ•γ) − X(ζ•d(K₀γ)).
 - First term. (ζ•γ − γ)(x) = (ζ(x) − 1)•γ(x) = 0 for x ∈ spt X. By (0a) and linearity, X(ζ•γ) = X(γ).
 - Second term. On the open set N, ψ = K₀γ because ζ ≡ 1 there. So for x ∈ N, ψ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] K₀γ, hence Dψ(x) = D(K₀γ)(x) (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq) and dψ(x) = d(K₀γ)(x) = ζ(x)•d(K₀γ)(x). Thus the test form ζ•d(K₀γ) − dψ vanishes on N ⊇ spt X, and (0a) gives X(ζ•d(K₀γ)) = X(dψ).
 - X(dψ) = (∂X)(ψ) = 0 because ∂X = 0.
 Hence ∂Y(γ) = X(γ) for every γ, and Y.boundary = X by extensionality (GeometricCurrentOn.ext).
6. Support (step 6 of the parent proof). Let C₀ := {s•x : s ∈ [0,1], x ∈ spt X}. It is the image of the compact set [0,1] × spt X under the continuous map (s, x) ↦ s•x, so it is compact and closed.
 (6a) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{k+1} with tsupport ω ∩ C₀ = ∅. For x ∈ spt X and t ∈ [0,1], t•x ∈ C₀, so ω(t•x) = 0. So the integrand t ↦ t^k • (ω(t•x)).curryLeft x vanishes for every t ∈ [0,1], and the interval integral over [0,1] is 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_congr on uIcc 0 1 with the zero function). Hence Kω(x) = 0 and η_ω(x) = 0 for every x ∈ spt X, and (0a) gives Y(ω) = X(η_ω) = 0.
 (6b) Let y ∉ C₀. Since C₀ is closed, there is r > 0 with ball(y, r) ∩ C₀ = ∅. Put W := ball(y, r).
  - W is open, and closure W ⊆ closedBall(y, r) is compact (ℝ^P is proper) and ⊆ univ.
  - Y vanishes on W: if tsupport ω ⊆ W, then tsupport ω ∩ C₀ = ∅, so Y(ω) = 0 by (6a).
  - Hence W ⊆ Y.zeroRegion, and y ∈ W, so y ∉ Y.support = univ ∖ Y.zeroRegion.
 Thus Y.support ⊆ C₀ = {y | ∃ s ∈ Icc 0 1, ∃ x ∈ X.support, y = s•x}. Y.support is closed (the complement of the open zero region), so as a closed subset of the compact C₀ it is compact.
7. Steps 3–6 give Y with Y.boundary = X, IsCompact Y.support, Y.support ⊆ C₀, and the action formula. ∎
proof_key_steps: From R (carrier ⊆ spt X, finite mass): X(γ) = 0 when γ vanishes on spt X, and |X(γ)| ≤ μ_R(ℝ^P)·sup‖γ‖ since unit orientations have norm ≤ 1.
With a bump ζ ≡ 1 on ball(0,ρ) ⊇ spt X and K smooth (sibling radial_homotopy), η_ω := ζ·Kω is a test form linear in ω. Y(ω) := X(η_ω) is a current, since ‖η_{ω_j}‖ ≤ (ρ+1) sup‖ω_j‖ → 0.
∂Y(γ) = X(ζ K(dγ)) = X(ζγ) − X(ζ d(K₀γ)) by the homotopy formula. Since ζ ≡ 1 near spt X, d is local, and ∂X = 0, this equals X(γ) − X(d(ζK₀γ)) = X(γ).
If tsupport ω misses the compact cone C₀, then Kω = 0 on spt X, so Y(ω) = 0. Hence spt Y ⊆ C₀, and spt Y is compact.
